question: In a roof truss design, two beams are placed such that one makes an angle theta with the horizontal and the other makes (90° - theta ). If sin theta = 0.6, what is the value of sin² theta + cos²(90° - theta )?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **trigonometric identity** for **complementary angles**: cos(90° − θ) = sin θ.

Substitute this into the expression: sin² θ + cos²(90° − θ) = sin² θ + sin² θ.

The simplified expression is 2 × sin² θ.

Given sin θ = 0.6, the value is 2 × (0.6)² = 2 × 0.36 = 0.72.

**∴ The correct answer is 0.72.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Angle of first beam = θ

Angle of second beam = 90° − θ

Value of **sin θ = 0.6**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d35917a319594ba4d9f2cf5d5ed93047c0b3ea9849c29b669a61f12be316fd9a.png] 

**Formula Used:**

1. Trigonometric identity for complementary angles: **cos(90° − θ) = sin θ**

2. Algebraic substitution: **(x)² = x²**

**Calculations:**

⇒ sin θ = 0.6

⇒ cos(90° − θ) = sin θ = 0.6

⇒ sin² θ = (0.6)² = 0.36

⇒ cos²(90° − θ) = (0.6)² = 0.36

⇒ sin² θ + cos²(90° − θ) = 0.36 + 0.36

⇒ Total Value = 0.72

**∴ The correct answer is 0.72.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angle Identities

For any angle θ, sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Pythagorean Identity

The fundamental identity in trigonometry is sin² θ + cos² θ = 1, which relates the sine and cosine of the same angle.

Standard Triplets

If sin θ = 0.6 (which is 3/5), then cos θ = 0.8 (which is 4/5), following the 3-4-5 right-angled triangle ratio.</p
